nodes.summary: Let $E_n$ denote the Euler coefficients, let $e^x$ be the exponential series, and let $e^{-x}$ be the series obtained from it by replacing $x$ with $-x$. In the ring $\mathbb{Q}[[x]]$ of formal power series with rational coefficients, $(e^x + e^{-x}) \sum_{n \ge 0} E_n x^n / n! = 2 + e^x - e^{-x}$.
nodes.title: Exponential generating function of the Euler coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $E_m$ denote the Euler coefficients, and let $\varepsilon_m$ be $1$ if $m$ is odd and $0$ if $m$ is even. For every natural number $n$, $E_{n+1} = \varepsilon_{n+1} - \sum_j \binom{n+1}{j} E_{n+1-j}$, where the sum runs over the even $j$ with $2 \le j \le n+1$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the Euler coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $\varepsilon_n$ be $1$ if $n$ is odd and $0$ if $n$ is even. The Euler coefficients $E_n$ are the integers defined by $E_0 = 1$ and, for $n \ge 1$, $E_n = \varepsilon_n - \sum_j \binom{n}{j} E_{n-j}$, where the sum runs over the even $j$ with $2 \le j \le n$.
nodes.title: Euler coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $\varepsilon_N$ be $1$ if $N$ is odd and $0$ if $N$ is even. For each natural number $n$, this is the list $[c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n]$ of integers with $c_0 = 1$ and, for $1 \le N \le n$, $c_N = \varepsilon_N - \sum_j \binom{N}{j} c_{N-j}$, where the sum runs over the even $j$ with $2 \le j \le N$. The Euler coefficient $E_n$ is its last entry $c_n$. The list is built one entry at a time, so each step reuses the…
nodes.title: The list of the first Euler coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $E_m$ denote the Euler coefficients. This is the integer sequence $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ with $a_0 = 0$ and $a_m = E_m$ for $m \ge 1$. It is the initial row of the Euler–Seidel matrix from which the median Euler numbers are read off.
nodes.title: Initial row for the median Euler numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the median Euler number $R_n$ is divisible by $3$, and $R_n / 3 \equiv 3^{n-1} \pmod 5$.
nodes.title: Median Euler numbers modulo three and five

nodes.summary: Let $E_m$ denote the Euler coefficients, and let $(a_n^k)$ be the Euler–Seidel matrix of the initial row $a_0 = 0$, $a_m = E_m$ for $m \ge 1$, so that $a_n^0 = a_n$ and $a_n^{k+1} = a_n^k + a_{n+1}^k$. The median Euler number $R_n$ is the natural number $|a_{n+1}^n|$. Equivalently, $R_n = \left|\sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} E_{n+1+i}\right|$.
nodes.title: Median Euler numbers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
